day_shape: 90 items: Iran claims drone/missile strikes on US bases in Bahrain, Kuwait and Jordan in 24th 'Saaeqa' phase; CENTCOM confirms 13th consecutive night of strikes and naval blockade redirecting 12 vessels; Hormuz traffic drops to one tanker as oil tops $100; Iran reportedly rejects Trump ceasefire relayed via Iraqi PM.

threads.label: Iranian strikes on Gulf US bases
threads.summary: Regime channels announced a 24th phase of 'Operation Saaeqa' with drone and missile strikes claimed on Sheikh Isa base in Bahrain, Ali Al-Salem in Kuwait and sites in Jordan, with sirens reported in Kuwait. The Jerusalem Post cited reports of damage to US living quarters, drone shelters and radar systems across the region.

threads.label: US strikes and naval blockade of Iran
threads.summary: CENTCOM said US forces began a 13th consecutive night of strikes on Iranian military targets at 18:45 ET and had redirected 12 commercial vessels and disabled one since resuming the naval blockade nine days earlier. Iranian officials reported American missile strikes on Piranshahr, Bandar Anzali and Bandar Abbas, with power lines damaged in Hormozgan.

threads.label: Hormuz shipping and oil price shock
threads.summary: Iran International and the Jerusalem Post reported Strait of Hormuz tanker traffic fell to one vessel Thursday, the lowest since 7 May, with oil rising above $100 after Houthi attacks on two Saudi tankers in the Red Sea. Iran International said Chinese customs data indicated Iran's own China trade had been hit harder than Beijing's other Gulf commerce.

threads.label: Ceasefire proposal and Iraq mediation
threads.summary: The Jerusalem Post reported Iran rejected a Trump ceasefire proposal delivered by Iraqi PM Ali al-Zaidi, citing unresolved control of the Strait of Hormuz, while Iran International reported Trump moving closer to a major new operation and further sanctions. Iraqi PM Zaidi met President Pezeshkian and Judiciary head Mohseni-Ejei in Tehran on regional security, trade and energy.

threads.label: Israel posture and Iran plots
threads.summary: Defence Minister Israel Katz warned any Iranian attack on Israel would draw a 'crushing' response after a high-level security consultation, with the IDF Arabic spokesperson saying it was prepared to return to combat. The PMO announced Mossad had foiled an Iranian Intelligence Ministry attempt to infiltrate a terror cell into Israel; a shooting near Havat Gilad wounded four.

threads.label: Iranian leadership messaging and diplomacy
threads.summary: Khamenei's office issued messages on 'retribution' and 'sacred unity,' while Foreign Minister Araghchi at the SCO foreign ministers' meeting called for the bloc to defend international law and denounced 'normalising crimes.' Admiral Sayyari and former IRGC commander Rezai issued statements dismissing Trump's threats.

threads.label: Iran domestic strain and Europe friction
threads.summary: Iran International reported unpaid wages leaving Iranian workers roughly two months from crisis and Russia's gasoline imports tightening Iran's 30-million-litre daily shortfall, while the Jerusalem Post noted continued execution of January protest defendants. France's Foreign Minister Barrot said two French diplomats detained in Tehran for nearly four hours, one allegedly beaten, had returned home.

events.title: A Hamas terrorist who invaded Israel during the October 7 onslaught and two other members of the terror group were killed in an Israeli strike in the Gaza Strip this week, the IDF and Shin Bet announce. The strike on Tuesday in the Strip's north targeted Abdallah Jahja, a member of Hamas's naval force. The IDF says that Jahja invaded Israel on October 7 and during the war and recently advanced attacks "in the maritime domain" against Israeli troops and civilians. Alongside Jahja, the army says that two other Hamas operatives were killed in the strike: Mohammed Al-Hawari and Sabhi Saqallah, both members of the Zeitoun Battalion.
